create_conversation.title: Start a conversation
create_conversation.description: Create a new conversation and get back the id every other tool needs. This is how a bot opens a proactive 1:1 chat: pass the target user in `members` along with the bot itself, and Teams either creates the chat or returns the existing one. Replying to an inbound message needs no creation -- reuse the `conversation.id` from the activity instead.

members.description: The ChannelAccounts to include, each at least {"id": "29:..."}. For a 1:1 chat this is the single target user.

is_group.description: True for a group conversation, false or omitted for 1:1.

topic_name.description: Topic for a group conversation, where the channel shows one.

tenant_id.description: The Microsoft Entra tenant the conversation belongs to.

channel_data.description: Teams-specific payload, e.g. {"tenant": {"id": "..."}} or a channel to post into.

activity.description: An Activity to send as soon as the conversation exists, saving a second call.

output.description: The new conversation's id, and the id of the activity if one was sent.

id.description: conversationId -- what every other tool takes.

get_conversations.title: List the bot's conversations
get_conversations.description: Page through the conversations this bot has taken part in. Continuation is by token rather than offset -- pass the previous response's `continuationToken` to get the next page. Useful for auditing reach; not a substitute for storing conversation ids as you learn them.

continuation_token.description: Token from the previous response, to fetch the next page.

output.description: A page of conversations the bot participates in.

send_to_conversation.title: Send a message to a conversation
send_to_conversation.description: Append an activity to a conversation -- the ordinary way a bot sends a message. Pass an Activity object; the common case is {"type": "message", "text": "..."} , and `attachments` carries Adaptive Cards. To answer a specific earlier message in a thread, use reply_to_activity instead.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id, from an inbound activity's conversation.id or from create_conversation.

output.description: The id of the activity that was sent.

reply_to_activity.title: Reply to a specific activity
reply_to_activity.description: Send an activity as a reply to an earlier one, which is what keeps a conversation threaded in a Teams channel. Where a channel does not support nested replies the message is simply appended, so this is always at least as good as send_to_conversation for answering a user.

activity_id.description: The id of the activity being replied to -- the inbound activity's `id`.

activity.description: The Activity to send as the reply.

output.description: The id of the reply activity.

update_activity.title: Edit an activity already sent
update_activity.description: Replace an activity the bot previously sent, which is how a card is redrawn after a user clicks one of its buttons. The whole Activity is replaced, not patched, so send the complete new body. Only works for the bot's own messages.

activity_id.description: The id of the activity to replace, as returned when it was sent.

output.description: The id of the updated activity.

delete_activity.title: Delete an activity
delete_activity.description: Remove an activity from a conversation. Irreversible, and it removes the message for everyone in the conversation, not just the bot's view. Only works for the bot's own messages and only where the channel supports deletion.

activity_id.description: The id of the activity to delete.

output.description: Empty on success; the status code carries the outcome.

send_conversation_history.title: Upload conversation history
send_conversation_history.description: Post a Transcript -- a batch of past activities -- into a conversation so the client can render them. Used when a bot migrates a conversation from elsewhere and wants the backlog visible, rather than for ordinary sending.

activities.description: The past Activity objects to render, oldest first.

output.description: The id assigned to the uploaded transcript.

get_activity_members.title: List the members of an activity
get_activity_members.description: The accounts involved in one specific activity within a conversation. Narrower than the conversation roster: it answers who a particular message concerned, which matters for member-added and member-removed events.

get_conversation_members.title: List a conversation's members
get_conversation_members.description: The full roster of a conversation in one response. Fine for 1:1 and small group chats; for a team or channel Microsoft says to use get_conversation_paged_members instead, because a large roster can come back incomplete or throttled here.

aadObjectId.description: Entra object id -- the join key to Microsoft Graph.

get_conversation_paged_members.title: List a conversation's members, one page at a time
get_conversation_paged_members.description: The roster in pages, which is the supported way to read a team or channel membership. Page size may be 50-500 and defaults to 200; loop on the returned `continuationToken` until it comes back empty. Paging is not available in 1:1 or group chats, where the whole roster is returned.

continuation_token.description: Token from the previous page; omit for the first.

output.description: One page of members plus the token for the next.

get_conversation_member.title: Get one conversation member
get_conversation_member.description: Details for a single member of a conversation, including the `aadObjectId` that joins them to their Microsoft Entra identity. Cheaper than pulling the whole roster when you already have the member id off an inbound activity's `from.id`.

member_id.description: The member's channel account id, e.g. the inbound activity's from.id.

delete_conversation_member.title: Remove a member from a conversation
delete_conversation_member.description: Remove someone from a conversation. If they were the last member the conversation is deleted along with them, so this can destroy the whole thread rather than just trimming its roster.

member_id.description: The channel account id of the member to remove.

output.description: Empty on success; the status code carries the outcome.

upload_attachment.title: Upload an attachment to a channel's store
upload_attachment.description: Put a file into the channel's own blob storage and get back an attachment id that get_attachment_info and get_attachment then read. Keeps the data inside the channel's compliance boundary instead of hosting it yourself. Contents go inline as base64 in `originalBase64`.

conversation_id.description: The conversation to store the attachment against.

output.description: The attachment id, for use with the attachment read tools.

get_attachment_info.title: Get an attachment's metadata
get_attachment_info.description: Name, content type and the list of available views for one attachment. Read this first: the view ids it returns ("original", "thumbnail") are what get_attachment takes, and guessing them is how that call 404s.

attachment_id.description: The attachment id, from upload_attachment or an inbound activity.

output.description: The attachment's metadata and available views.

get_attachment.title: Download an attachment view
get_attachment.description: Fetch one view of an attachment as binary content. The view id comes from get_attachment_info -- usually "original" for the full file or "thumbnail" for the preview.

view_id.description: The view to fetch, from get_attachment_info -- typically "original" or "thumbnail".

output.description: The attachment's binary content for that view.

get_team_details.title: Get a team's details
get_team_details.description: Teams-only extension: the team's name and its Microsoft Entra group id, which is the join key to Microsoft Graph's group and channel APIs. The `teamId` comes from an inbound activity's `channelData.team.id`; this answers nothing for a 1:1 or group chat.

team_id.description: The team id, from an inbound activity's channelData.team.id.

output.description: The team's id, name and Entra group id.

get_team_channels.title: List a team's channels
get_team_channels.description: Teams-only extension: the channels in a team, each with the conversation id to post into. Two quirks worth expecting -- the General channel's name comes back null so clients can localise it, and its channel id is always identical to the team id.

team_id.description: The team id, from an inbound activity's channelData.team.id.

output.description: The team's channels, each usable as a conversation id.
